method: live AudioContext on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.5) and the Android API 35 arm64 emulator, React Native 0.86.3 + React Native Audio API 0.13.3, Release builds; signals observed through an AnalyserNode (smoothing 0) with the audible path muted; two launches per platform, identical payloads; headless Chrome as control

fanin-live.reading: two simultaneous constant sources into one GainNode are summed correctly on every host

fanout-live.reading: a source connected to two gains (1 and 0.5) that reconverge delivers only the last-connected branch natively (0.25 × 0.5)

fanout-gain-live.reading: the same defect when the branching node is a GainNode; fan-out from any node keeps one outgoing edge

delay-live.reading: with two separate sources (no fan-out) the native live DelayNode delays exactly 480 frames; the offline zero-delay result is offline-only

version1Note: The version-1 delay probe (single source fanned out to dry and delayed paths) lost its dry impulses natively — values [0.5] only — which is the fan-out defect, not a delay defect. Retained as v1-native-results-*.json.
conclusions: Live native graphs sum fan-in correctly, so polyphonic voices into one filter or bus are sound; native polyphony is not blocked.

Live native graphs deliver only one outgoing connection per node. Every parallel wet/dry structure (Delay, Reverb) and every user-level fan-out is broken on this host; the offline results were the same defect plus offline-only summation/delay failures.

The native live DelayNode works; the offline DelayNode does not. Native offline rendering through the host graph is unusable beyond single chains, so deterministic offline rendering must be TuneJS-owned.

Decision: declare fan-out as a host limit in the adapter, reject a second outgoing connection and the wet/dry effects on such hosts with UNSUPPORTED (no silent substitution), and plan a TuneJS-owned single-node DSP path (worklet-based, shared JS DSP) for effects, spatial rendering and offline rendering.
